title: SailPoint Admin Domain 4 questions (4.1, 4.2)
note: Original questions written for Delzar Certification Academy. Not from exam dumps or commercial banks; not affiliated with SailPoint.

questions.stem: A manager revokes an entitlement during a manager certification. When is the removal sent for provisioning?
choices: When the campaign's end date passes
At the next scheduled account aggregation
When the reviewer signs off the certification
As soon as the reviewer clicks Revoke on the item
questions.answer: When the reviewer signs off the certification
questions.explanation: Revocation decisions are acted on after the reviewer signs off, which creates the provisioning request. Aggregation only reads the source and never removes access by itself.

questions.stem: An employee transfers to Finance, and the Finance role uses membership criteria on department. What causes the role's access to be provisioned?
choices: Identity processing re-evaluates role membership after the department attribute changes
An administrator must run a Create Account task
The role owner must approve the new member
The employee must submit an access request for the role, and the manager must approve it
questions.answer: Identity processing re-evaluates role membership after the department attribute changes
questions.explanation: Roles with membership criteria are assigned automatically when identity processing sees that the identity now matches, and their access profiles are then provisioned. No request or approval is needed.

questions.stem: HR marks a worker as terminated and the identity's lifecycle state becomes inactive. Which provisioning can this trigger?
choices: Deleting the identity from the tenant immediately
Removing the access profiles and disabling the accounts set for that lifecycle state
Starting a certification campaign so the worker's manager reviews all of the access first
Resetting the identity profile's priority
questions.answer: Removing the access profiles and disabling the accounts set for that lifecycle state
questions.explanation: A lifecycle state can remove access profiles, enable or disable accounts and send emails when an identity enters it. It does not delete the identity or start campaigns.

questions.stem: A user requests an access profile that needs manager and source owner approval. When does provisioning to the target begin?
choices: As soon as the user submits the request
At the next nightly identity refresh
After the manager approves, while the source owner reviews
After the final required approval is given
questions.answer: After the final required approval is given
questions.explanation: An access request is provisioned only once every approval step in its scheme is complete. Partial approval leaves the request pending.

questions.stem: Which of these is an automated provisioning trigger rather than one started by a person?
choices: A lifecycle state change calculated from HR data
A revocation made in a certification
An access request submitted by a user
A request a manager submits for a direct report
questions.answer: A lifecycle state change calculated from HR data
questions.explanation: Lifecycle states and role membership criteria drive automated provisioning from identity data. Access requests and certification decisions are user-initiated.

questions.stem: A Helpdesk user needs an Active Directory account disabled immediately while HR finishes paperwork. What can trigger this directly?
choices: Editing the source's account schema
Running an entitlement aggregation
Disabling the account from the identity's Accounts tab
Changing the account deletion threshold on the source
questions.answer: Disabling the account from the identity's Accounts tab
questions.explanation: Admins can act on an identity's accounts, for example disable or enable them, which sends a provisioning request to the source. Aggregations and schema edits do not change target accounts.

questions.stem: A workflow runs when an identity's manager changes and revokes a sensitive access profile. What does the workflow's access action produce?
choices: A search subscription email with the results
A new certification campaign for the old manager to confirm the removal
A change to the identity profile mappings
A provisioning request that removes the access on the source
questions.answer: A provisioning request that removes the access on the source
questions.explanation: Workflow actions that manage access submit requests that go through normal provisioning. They do not edit identity profiles or launch campaigns.

questions.stem: When does Identity Security Cloud use a source's Create Account policy?
choices: During every account aggregation
When an identity is granted access on a source where it has no account
When an existing account is disabled
Whenever an account attribute changes on the source and is aggregated again
questions.answer: When an identity is granted access on a source where it has no account
questions.explanation: The Create Account definition supplies attribute values for a brand-new account. Access added to an existing account is a modify operation.

questions.stem: New hires receive an Active Directory birthright role, but account creation fails because a required naming attribute is missing. What should the administrator fix?
choices: Add the attribute to the access profile's description
Add the attribute to the identity profile's priority list
Raise the source's account deletion threshold
Add the required attribute to the source's Create Account policy
questions.answer: Add the required attribute to the source's Create Account policy
questions.explanation: The target requires the attribute when the account is created, so the Create Account policy must supply a value for it. Access profile descriptions and thresholds are not sent to the target.

questions.stem: Two employees named Ana Silva join on the same day. What should the Create Account policy use so their new usernames do not collide?
choices: A generator that creates a unique account ID from a pattern
The manager's username with a suffix that the source owner types in by hand
A static value shared by both accounts
The identity's display name copied as is
questions.answer: A generator that creates a unique account ID from a pattern
questions.explanation: A unique account ID generator checks for existing values and adds a counter or other variation. Static or copied values would create duplicates.

questions.stem: A Create Account policy maps the account's department to the identity's department attribute. A new account is created with an empty department. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The source's VA was in the Busy state
The identity's department attribute was empty when the account was created
Create Account policies cannot take values from identity attributes, only static ones
The account was created by an access request
questions.answer: The identity's department attribute was empty when the account was created
questions.explanation: Mapped values are taken from the identity when the account is provisioned, so a blank identity attribute produces a blank account value. Fixing the identity data or mapping fixes future accounts.

questions.stem: A user who already has an account on a source is granted an access profile on that source. Is the Create Account policy used?
choices: No, the access is held until the next aggregation
Yes, a second account is always created
No, the entitlements are added to the existing account
Yes, the existing account is recreated with new values
questions.answer: No, the entitlements are added to the existing account
questions.explanation: Create Account applies only when there is no account to modify. Sources that allow several accounts per identity use access profile account options instead.

questions.stem: Where does an administrator define the attributes and values that new accounts on a source receive?
choices: In the identity profile's Mappings tab
In the access profile's approval settings
In the VA cluster's Edit page
In the source's Create Account configuration
questions.answer: In the source's Create Account configuration
questions.explanation: Each source has its own Create Account definition used when accounts are provisioned. Identity profile mappings build identity attributes, not account attributes.

questions.stem: A new source supports provisioning, but no one has reviewed its Create Account policy yet. What is the BEST practice before turning on birthright roles?
choices: Review and test the Create Account policy in the sandbox tenant
Delete the policy so the connector picks defaults
Turn on the roles in production and fix each account creation failure as it appears
Assign the roles to every identity at once
questions.answer: Review and test the Create Account policy in the sandbox tenant
questions.explanation: SailPoint recommends reviewing Create Account for each source and testing provisioning in sandbox first. Testing in production risks bad accounts for real users.

questions.stem: What does attribute sync do in Identity Security Cloud?
choices: Synchronizes passwords across all sources
Schedules aggregations to run at the same time
Pushes changes in identity attributes to the mapped account attributes on sources
Copies account attributes from every source into the matching identity attributes
questions.answer: Pushes changes in identity attributes to the mapped account attributes on sources
questions.explanation: Attribute sync keeps account data on target sources aligned with identity data in the tenant. Pulling source data into identity attributes is the identity profile's job.

questions.stem: An employee's last name changes in the HR source, but the surname in Active Directory stays the same. What should the administrator configure?
choices: A new Create Account policy on the HR source
Attribute sync for the surname on the Active Directory source
A certification of Active Directory accounts
A higher priority for Active Directory in the identity profile
questions.answer: Attribute sync for the surname on the Active Directory source
questions.explanation: Create Account values are only used when an account is created; attribute sync updates existing accounts when the identity attribute changes. Changing priorities would not write to AD.

questions.stem: What starts an attribute sync update to a target account?
choices: An account aggregation that finds a different value on the target account than before
A change to the mapped identity attribute found during identity processing
A reviewer approving an access request
A VA restart
questions.answer: A change to the mapped identity attribute found during identity processing
questions.explanation: Attribute sync reacts to changes in the identity attribute, which identity processing detects. Aggregations read accounts; they do not push values.

questions.stem: An administrator wants attribute sync on a delimited file source. Why will this not update the file's system?
choices: Attribute sync works only on authoritative sources
Delimited file sources cannot be mapped to identity attributes in an identity profile
The source is not direct-connect and has no automated provisioning
Attribute sync requires a SaaS connector
questions.answer: The source is not direct-connect and has no automated provisioning
questions.explanation: Attribute sync writes through the connector, so the source must be a provisioning-capable direct connection. Flat file sources only receive manual tasks.

questions.stem: How do Create Account and attribute sync differ for a source?
choices: Create Account sets initial values; attribute sync keeps them updated afterwards
Both are configured on the identity profile
Both run only during account aggregation
Attribute sync creates the accounts; Create Account updates their values afterwards
questions.answer: Create Account sets initial values; attribute sync keeps them updated afterwards
questions.explanation: Create Account fills in a new account's attributes once, and attribute sync later pushes identity changes. Both are configured per source.

questions.stem: After enabling attribute sync for title on a source, an administrator wants to confirm an update reached the target. Where should the administrator look?
choices: The VA cluster's Cluster Components page
The identity profile's preview
The access profile's approval history
The identity's account activity in Search
questions.answer: The identity's account activity in Search
questions.explanation: Attribute updates are recorded as account activity with status, stage and any errors. The identity profile preview shows identity calculations, not provisioning results.

questions.stem: Attribute sync for email is on for a source, yet the account was never updated after the identity's email changed. What should the administrator check FIRST?
choices: Whether the VA cluster's time zone matches
Whether the source has a scheduled entitlement aggregation
Whether the identity has a pending certification
Whether provisioning is enabled on the source
questions.answer: Whether provisioning is enabled on the source
questions.explanation: Attribute sync is provisioning, so a source left read-only cannot receive the update. Schedules and time zones do not block writes.

questions.stem: An administrator wants a direct-connect source to stop writing to its target and send manual work items instead. What should the administrator change?
choices: Disconnect the source from its VA cluster so changes cannot reach the target
Turn off Enable Provisioning in the source's Base Configuration
Delete the source's Create Account policy
Remove the source owner
questions.answer: Turn off Enable Provisioning in the source's Base Configuration
questions.explanation: Without the provisioning feature the source is read-only and changes become manual work items. Deleting the policy or the VA link would break other functions.

questions.stem: Using the API, how can an administrator check whether a source has provisioning turned on?
choices: Get the source and look for PROVISIONING in its features list
Get the source's account schema and look for a write flag
Search account activity for the source's name
List the VA clusters and look for the source name
questions.answer: Get the source and look for PROVISIONING in its features list
questions.explanation: The Get Source response lists the PROVISIONING feature when provisioning is enabled. The schema and cluster lists do not show this setting.

questions.stem: Which object do roles and lifecycle states use to grant a bundle of entitlements from one source?
choices: An identity profile
A transform
An access profile
A search subscription
questions.answer: An access profile
questions.explanation: Access profiles bundle entitlements from a single source and are granted by roles, lifecycle states and requests. Identity profiles and transforms build identity data.

questions.stem: Some identities have two accounts on the same source. How can an administrator control which account receives access from an access profile during automated provisioning?
choices: Edit the identity profile so the source becomes its authoritative source
Configure the access profile's multiple account options
Lower the source's deletion threshold
Rename one of the accounts
questions.answer: Configure the access profile's multiple account options
questions.explanation: Access profiles have options that decide which account gets the access when an identity has more than one. The identity profile does not choose target accounts.

questions.stem: Aggregations from a database source work, but every provisioning attempt fails with a permission error. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The VA cluster has two VAs
The identity profile that uses the source has the wrong priority set
The source's service account can read but not change the target
The source has no account correlation
questions.answer: The source's service account can read but not change the target
questions.explanation: Aggregation needs only read rights, while provisioning needs write rights on the target. Correlation and identity profile settings do not cause permission errors.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT needed for a role to provision an entitlement automatically to an Active Directory source?
choices: An access profile that contains the entitlement
A source with provisioning enabled
A role that includes the access profile
A certification campaign that includes the role
questions.answer: A certification campaign that includes the role
questions.explanation: Automated provisioning needs a provisioning-enabled source, the entitlement in an access profile and the profile in a role. Certifications review access but are not part of granting it.

questions.stem: A source's connector supports provisioning. What else determines whether a lifecycle state's provisioning is done automatically or as a manual task?
choices: Whether the source has a direct connection with provisioning enabled
Whether the lifecycle state is set to send an email notification to the manager
Whether the source is authoritative
Whether the identity has a manager
questions.answer: Whether the source has a direct connection with provisioning enabled
questions.explanation: Direct-connect sources with provisioning enabled are changed automatically, while flat file or read-only sources get manual tasks. Emails and managers do not change the channel.

questions.stem: Which list names the main provisioning channels in Identity Security Cloud?
choices: Roles, access profiles and entitlements
Search, reports and subscriptions
Direct connector, service desk integration and manual tasks
Account aggregation, account correlation and identity attribute transforms
questions.answer: Direct connector, service desk integration and manual tasks
questions.explanation: Changes reach targets through a connector, a service desk ticket or a manual task for a person. The other lists are data loading, access modeling and reporting features.

questions.stem: A delimited file source is assigned an access profile through a role. Who receives the manual provisioning task for an entitlement change?
choices: The entitlement owner, with the source owner as fallback
The tenant administrator who created the role that granted the access profile
The identity that receives the access
The identity's manager
questions.answer: The entitlement owner, with the source owner as fallback
questions.explanation: Manual tasks for entitlements go to the entitlement owner and fall back to the source owner. Managers approve requests but do not do manual provisioning.

questions.stem: A company runs ServiceNow and wants changes to a disconnected application handled as tickets by its IT team. Which channel fits BEST?
choices: A scheduled search report
A service desk integration
A direct connector on a VA
A manual task in the Task Manager
questions.answer: A service desk integration
questions.explanation: Service desk integration turns provisioning actions into tickets in the ITSM tool so existing teams fulfil them. Manual tasks are worked in ISC instead.

questions.stem: Which provisioning channel gives near real-time automated changes with no human involvement?
choices: A manual task assigned to the source owner in the Task Manager
A certification campaign
A service desk integration
A direct connector, either VA-based or SaaS
questions.answer: A direct connector, either VA-based or SaaS
questions.explanation: Direct connectors write to the target as soon as the request is processed. Tickets and manual tasks depend on people completing them.

questions.stem: A small legacy app has no API, only 15 users and no ticketing process. Which channel is MOST practical?
choices: A service desk integration
A custom direct connector built for the app
Attribute sync on the source
Manual tasks assigned to the source owner
questions.answer: Manual tasks assigned to the source owner
questions.explanation: With no API and no ITSM tool, manual tasks let a person make the change and mark it complete. Building a connector is not worth it for 15 users.

questions.stem: A governance group owns a disconnected source. How does this affect manual provisioning tasks for it?
choices: Tasks are sent to SailPoint Support instead of a person in the group
The task can show multiple owners from the group
Tasks are created only after aggregation
The source becomes direct-connect
questions.answer: The task can show multiple owners from the group
questions.explanation: When a governance group is associated with a disconnected source, the task lists multiple owners who can work it. It does not change the source type.

questions.stem: After a service desk ticket is closed in ServiceNow, how does Identity Security Cloud learn that the change is done?
choices: ServiceNow writes directly to the identity profile
The change is assumed done as soon as the ticket is created in ServiceNow
It checks the ticket's status through the service desk integration
The source owner must aggregate the source manually
questions.answer: It checks the ticket's status through the service desk integration
questions.explanation: The integration periodically checks ticket status and updates the account activity when the ticket closes. A ticket's creation does not mean the change is complete.

questions.stem: Match each situation to the provisioning channel that fits it BEST.

pairs.item: On-premises Active Directory reached through a VA
Disconnected app whose changes the IT team handles as ServiceNow tickets
Legacy app with no API and a handful of users
Cloud app with a SaaS connector

questions.explanation: Connected systems are changed by connectors, ITSM-driven teams by tickets and small disconnected apps by manual tasks. A search report only shows data.

questions.stem: A new hire's HR record is aggregated and a birthright role grants Active Directory access. Put the events in order.
items: The HR source aggregation creates the identity
Identity processing calculates attributes and the lifecycle state
The role's membership criteria match and the role is assigned
The Create Account policy builds the new account's attributes
The VA's connector creates the account in Active Directory
questions.explanation: Identity data comes first, then role assignment, then the account is built from Create Account and written by the connector. Without the identity and role there is nothing to provision.

questions.stem: A role must grant an Active Directory group automatically. Which TWO items must be in place on the source side?
choices: Provisioning enabled on the source
An access profile containing the group
A certification campaign on the source
A search subscription on the group
Enable Debugging on the cluster
answers: An access profile containing the group
questions.explanation: The source must allow provisioning and the entitlement must be in an access profile that the role includes. Certifications and subscriptions are governance and reporting features.

questions.stem: Which connector log level is the MOST verbose?
choices: TRACE
WARN
DEBUG
INFO
questions.answer: TRACE
questions.explanation: From least to most detail the levels are ERROR, WARN, INFO, DEBUG and TRACE. TRACE is finer than DEBUG.

questions.stem: Which log level records only errors that may still let the connector continue?
choices: TRACE
ERROR
INFO
DEBUG
questions.answer: ERROR
questions.explanation: ERROR is the least verbose level and shows error events. INFO adds coarse progress messages.

questions.stem: An administrator needs detailed logs for Active Directory provisioning only. Which logging class should be raised?
choices: sailpoint.connector.JDBCConnector
sailpoint.connector.WebServices
sailpoint.connector.ADLDAPConnector
sailpoint.connector.DelimitedFileConnector
questions.answer: sailpoint.connector.ADLDAPConnector
questions.explanation: The AD connector's main class is sailpoint.connector.ADLDAPConnector. The others belong to JDBC, Web Services and delimited file connectors.

questions.stem: In a cluster log configuration, what is the difference between rootLevel and logLevels?
choices: rootLevel is the default for all logs; logLevels sets levels for named classes
rootLevel applies to Windows-based sources; logLevels applies to Linux-based sources
rootLevel sets duration; logLevels sets file size
rootLevel controls the VA OS; logLevels controls the tenant
questions.answer: rootLevel is the default for all logs; logLevels sets levels for named classes
questions.explanation: rootLevel is the default level for everything, and logLevels maps logging classes to their own levels. Duration is a separate field.

questions.stem: A JDBC provisioning issue needs detail, but the team wants to avoid huge logs from other connectors. What is the BEST setting?
choices: Set rootLevel to TRACE for the whole cluster
Enable Debugging on every VA cluster in the tenant for the next 24 hours
Set rootLevel to ERROR and logLevels to empty
Keep rootLevel at INFO and set sailpoint.connector.JDBCConnector to DEBUG
questions.answer: Keep rootLevel at INFO and set sailpoint.connector.JDBCConnector to DEBUG
questions.explanation: Raising only the JDBC class gives detail for the problem connector and keeps other logs small. A TRACE root level would flood the disk.

questions.stem: A Web Services source fails during provisioning. Which logging class should be set to DEBUG to capture its detail?
choices: sailpoint.connector.LDAPConnector
sailpoint.connector.WebServices
sailpoint.connector.Office365Connector
sailpoint.connector.ADLDAPConnector
questions.answer: sailpoint.connector.WebServices
questions.explanation: The Web Services connector logs under sailpoint.connector.WebServices. The AD and LDAP classes would not capture its calls.

questions.stem: An administrator will set connector log levels through the API. What must be found FIRST?
choices: The ID of the source owner
The ID of the identity profile that uses the source
The ID of the VA cluster, from the managed clusters list
The ID of the access profile
questions.answer: The ID of the VA cluster, from the managed clusters list
questions.explanation: Log configuration is set per VA cluster, so the cluster ID comes first from the list of managed clusters. Identity and access profile IDs are not involved.

questions.stem: A GET of a cluster's log configuration returns 204 No Content. What does this mean?
choices: The caller lacks permission to read the cluster's settings
The cluster ID is wrong
The cluster has no VAs
No log configuration is set, so a new one can be created
questions.answer: No log configuration is set, so a new one can be created
questions.explanation: A 204 means the cluster has no logging configuration yet; the admin can PUT a new one. A wrong ID or missing rights would return an error instead.

questions.stem: Which fields does the body of a cluster log configuration update contain?
choices: durationMinutes, rootLevel and logLevels
clusterName, timeZone and description
sourceId, accountId and password
cron, enabled and notifyEmail
questions.answer: durationMinutes, rootLevel and logLevels
questions.explanation: The update sets how long logging stays raised, the default level and per-class levels. Cluster name and time zone are edited elsewhere.

questions.stem: An administrator raised a connector's log level through the API a minute ago and sees no new detail. What is the MOST likely explanation?
choices: The setting applies only to SaaS connectors
The VA must be paired again first
The new levels take effect after about five minutes
Log levels only change after a reboot
questions.answer: The new levels take effect after about five minutes
questions.explanation: SailPoint notes that the cluster starts writing the new log detail about five minutes after the update. No re-pairing or reboot is needed.

questions.stem: After raising AD connector logging on a VA cluster, where does the administrator read the new log lines?
choices: In the identity profile's audit history for the affected user
In the Provisioning Activity report
In the source's Accounts tab
In ccg.log under /home/sailpoint/log on the VAs
questions.answer: In ccg.log under /home/sailpoint/log on the VAs
questions.explanation: Connector logs on VA-based sources are written to ccg.log on each VA. Reports and the UI show results, not connector debug detail.

questions.stem: Why does a cluster log configuration include a duration?
choices: So raised log levels turn off automatically and do not fill the disk
So the VA reboots when logging ends
So the logs already written are deleted after that many minutes pass
So SailPoint can bill for logging time
questions.answer: So raised log levels turn off automatically and do not fill the disk
questions.explanation: Raised logging ends after durationMinutes, protecting disk space and performance. Logs already written are kept.

questions.topic: Source Debug Logging and Connector Logs
questions.stem: Where does an administrator turn on debug logging for one source with an automatic expiry?
choices: The VA cluster's Cluster Components page
The source's Additional Settings > Administrator Settings
The Admin Dashboard's Tasks list
The identity profile's Provisioning tab for identities on the source
questions.answer: The source's Additional Settings > Administrator Settings
questions.explanation: Administrator Settings on the source offer a Debug Logging toggle with an expiry time. The VA cluster page has its own cluster-wide debugging option.

questions.topic: Source Debug Logging and Connector Logs
questions.stem: Why does source debug logging have an Expiry Time setting?
choices: So SailPoint receives the collected debug logs only after the expiry time passes
So debug logging turns off by itself when troubleshooting is done
So the source is disabled at the expiry
So debug logs are deleted after the expiry
questions.answer: So debug logging turns off by itself when troubleshooting is done
questions.explanation: The expiry automatically disables debug logging, preventing verbose logs from running forever. It does not delete logs or disable the source.

questions.topic: Source Debug Logging and Connector Logs
questions.stem: A provisioning error occurred on a SaaS connector source this morning. How can the administrator get the connector's logs?
choices: Export the identity's access history
Sign in to a VA and open ccg.log
Run an entitlement aggregation with the connector's log level set to TRACE
Generate connector logs for a time range on the source and download them
questions.answer: Generate connector logs for a time range on the source and download them
questions.explanation: SaaS sources run in SailPoint's cloud, so logs are generated from the source's Administrator Settings for a chosen range. There is no VA log for them.

questions.topic: Source Debug Logging and Connector Logs
questions.stem: When generating connector logs with a custom range, which limit applies?
choices: A range of 24 hours or less from the last 90 days
A range of up to 7 days from the last 30 days
Only the last hour
Any range up to one year
questions.answer: A range of 24 hours or less from the last 90 days
questions.explanation: Custom ranges can cover up to 24 hours within the last 90 days, and presets cover the last 24, 6 or 1 hours. Longer windows must be pulled in pieces.

questions.topic: Source Debug Logging and Connector Logs
questions.stem: After downloading generated connector logs, what does the administrator receive?
choices: A PDF report that is emailed to the source owner and the requester
A link to a live log stream in Search
A zip file to extract and open in a text editor
A CSV of identity attributes
questions.answer: A zip file to extract and open in a text editor
questions.explanation: The download is a zip of log files that can be read in any text or code editor. It is not a report or a search result.

questions.topic: Source Debug Logging and Connector Logs
questions.stem: A provisioning failure shows a short generic error in the UI. Which part of the connector log is MOST useful to search support articles with?
choices: The tenant name and the connector version at the top of the log file
The first INFO line of the day
Keywords from the inner error message near the failure time
The generic UI error text
questions.answer: Keywords from the inner error message near the failure time
questions.explanation: The inner message carries the target's actual error, such as an HTTP or LDAP code. The generic UI text matches too many unrelated problems.

questions.stem: An access request was approved but the user still lacks the access. Which object should the administrator search FIRST?
choices: The account activity for that request
The VA cluster's time zone
The identity profile
The access profile's description and its owner
questions.answer: The account activity for that request
questions.explanation: Account activity records each action on source accounts, with status, stage and errors for each account request. It shows exactly where provisioning stopped.

questions.stem: An account activity shows the status Incomplete. What does this mean?
choices: All actions completed
Every action failed
Nothing has been attempted yet, but it is scheduled
Some requested actions succeeded and some failed
questions.answer: Some requested actions succeeded and some failed
questions.explanation: Incomplete is a partial result. Pending means not yet attempted, Failure means all failed, and Complete means approved actions finished.

questions.stem: Which query finds account activities where every action failed?
choices: stage:completed
status:failure
status:pending
status:complete
questions.answer: status:failure
questions.explanation: The overall status Failure is searched with status:failure. Stage values describe progress, not success.

questions.stem: An account request inside an activity shows the result status Unverifiable. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The source owner rejected the change in a manual task on the source
The request is waiting for approval
The VA cluster is offline
The source's account schema lacks the attribute being provisioned
questions.answer: The source's account schema lacks the attribute being provisioned
questions.explanation: Unverifiable means the request was sent, but ISC cannot confirm it because the attribute is not in the account schema. Adding it to the schema lets results be verified.

questions.stem: An account activity's stage is Terminated. What does this mean?
choices: The action was cancelled and will not be retried
The action is waiting for its next retry after a failure
The action was confirmed on the source
The action is in progress
questions.answer: The action was cancelled and will not be retried
questions.explanation: Terminated is a final stage for cancelled actions. Executing means in progress and Completed means confirmed on the source.

questions.stem: An account request result shows Retry. What does Identity Security Cloud do next?
choices: It waits for an administrator to approve a retry from the account activity page
It tries the action again later because the failure was retryable
It creates a manual task for the identity
It deletes the account from the source
questions.answer: It tries the action again later because the failure was retryable
questions.explanation: Retry means the action failed with a retryable error and will be attempted again. Failed would mean no further retries.

questions.stem: An account request result shows Manual Task Created. What does this tell the administrator?
choices: The change was applied automatically to the target
The request was rejected by the approver
The source is not direct-connect, so a person must complete the change
The connector failed, so SailPoint opened a support case for the tenant administrator
questions.answer: The source is not direct-connect, so a person must complete the change
questions.explanation: Manual Task Created means a task was assigned to the source or entitlement owner. It is the expected result for disconnected sources.

questions.stem: An auditor wants a downloadable list of recent provisioning events with full details. Where should the administrator go?
choices: Admin > Connections > Virtual Appliances
Search > Reports > Provisioning Activity
Admin > Access Model > Roles
Admin > Identity Management > Identity Profiles
questions.answer: Search > Reports > Provisioning Activity
questions.explanation: The Provisioning Activity report lists provisioning events, opens details for each and can be downloaded. The other pages configure the tenant.

questions.stem: Which Search area shows audit events such as access requests, password changes and lifecycle state changes?
choices: Roles
Access Profiles
Entitlements
Events
questions.answer: Events
questions.explanation: Events cover audit activity, including categories such as access requests, account attribute updates and lifecycle state changes. The other areas search access objects.

questions.stem: For how long does the Account Activity tab show account activities?
choices: The past 7 days
The past 24 hours
The past 60 days
The past five years
questions.answer: The past 60 days
questions.explanation: The Account Activity view covers 60 days of activity, newest first by Last Modified. Older data needs other reports or exports.

questions.stem: In the Provisioning Activity report, how can the administrator see more fields in the grid before downloading?
choices: Use the Column Chooser to add columns
Edit the source's account schema
Change the identity profile mappings
Raise the connector's log level
questions.answer: Use the Column Chooser to add columns
questions.explanation: The Column Chooser in the report table adds columns to the grid. Schema and logging changes do not affect the report layout.

questions.stem: A user reports that an account lock happened unexpectedly yesterday. Which Search event category is MOST relevant?
choices: Identity Refresh
Workflow History
Account State Update
Certification
questions.answer: Account State Update
questions.explanation: Account State Update events record locking or unlocking accounts on sources. Identity Refresh covers identity recalculations.

questions.stem: Provisioning to a VA-based source fails with ConnectException. How does Identity Security Cloud handle it?
choices: It deletes the request immediately
It retries once per hour, up to three times
It retries every minute until it succeeds
It converts the request into a service desk ticket
questions.answer: It retries once per hour, up to three times
questions.explanation: ConnectException and NoRouteToHostException are retryable, so ISC retries hourly up to three times. Retries may be delayed by other work in the tenant queue.

questions.stem: Where can an administrator see manual provisioning tasks for everyone in the organization?
choices: Admin > Dashboard > Tasks
The source's Create Account page
Admin > Connections > Virtual Appliances
Search > Roles
questions.answer: Admin > Dashboard > Tasks
questions.explanation: The Tasks page lists manual tasks assigned to the admin and other users, filtered by To Do or Completed. The other pages do not track tasks.

questions.stem: A source owner is on leave and cannot complete a manual provisioning task. What should the administrator do?
choices: Mark the task complete without making the change
Change the source to direct-connect
Delete the task and wait for a new one
Use Actions > Reassign on the task
questions.answer: Use Actions > Reassign on the task
questions.explanation: Admins can reassign a task so someone else completes it. Marking it complete without the change would leave the record wrong.

questions.stem: A source owner has made a manual change in the target but forgot to close the task. How can an administrator close it?
choices: Run an account aggregation on the source
Use Actions > Mark as Complete on the task
Delete the account activity
Restart the VA cluster
questions.answer: Use Actions > Mark as Complete on the task
questions.explanation: Mark as Complete moves the task to the Completed list. Aggregation updates account data but does not close tasks.

questions.stem: Provisioning keeps failing with NoRouteToHostException after all retries. What should the administrator investigate?
choices: The identity profile's authoritative source and its attribute mappings
The certification campaign schedule
Network routing between the VA and the target system
The access profile's approval scheme
questions.answer: Network routing between the VA and the target system
questions.explanation: This exception means the VA could not reach the target host. It is a network problem, not an approval or identity setting.

questions.stem: A retryable provisioning failure was scheduled to retry in 60 minutes, but it ran later than that. What is the MOST likely reason?
choices: Other work items in the tenant's queue delayed it
The retry needs an administrator's approval before it runs again
Retries run only during the nightly refresh
The VA's time zone was changed
questions.answer: Other work items in the tenant's queue delayed it
questions.explanation: The retry is scheduled for an hour later but may wait behind other queued work. No approval or nightly window is involved.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order to raise Active Directory connector logging on a VA cluster with the API.
items: List the managed clusters and note the cluster ID
Get the cluster's current log configuration
Put a configuration with durationMinutes, rootLevel and the AD class in logLevels
Wait about five minutes and reproduce the problem
Read the new detail in ccg.log on the VAs
questions.explanation: The cluster is identified, its current settings read, then updated; after about five minutes the detail appears in ccg.log. Reproducing the problem afterwards captures the right lines.

questions.stem: Match each account request result status to its meaning.

pairs.match: The request was sent to the connector
The attribute is missing from the account schema
It failed but will be attempted again
It failed and will not be retried
A person must make the change

targets_extra: The request is waiting for manager approval
questions.explanation: Account request results track each source's part of an action. Approval waits belong to the access request, not to account request results.

questions.stem: An administrator is troubleshooting a failed provisioning action. Which TWO places in Search are MOST useful?
choices: Account Activity
The Provisioning Activity report
The Roles tab
The Access Profiles tab
The Entitlements tab
questions.explanation: Account Activity shows the status, stage and errors of each action, and the Provisioning Activity report lists provisioning events with details. Roles, access profiles and entitlements describe access, not what happened.
